cambridge.definitionEn: the range of matters considered or dealt with:

learning.title: 涉及或处理的范围
learning.en: the range of matters considered or dealt with:
learning.example: The scope excludes staff training.
learning.zh: 范围不包括员工培训。

history.summary: scope在16世纪已有行动余地、活动空间和目标等用法。它经意大利语进入英语，上溯表示目标、观察对象的希腊语；后来发展出思想所及范围和某种活动的领域等意义。

cambridge.definitionEn: something that must be completed or provided as part of a project:

learning.title: 项目中必须完成或提供的成果
learning.en: something that must be completed or provided as part of a project:
learning.example: The final deliverable is a test report.
learning.zh: 最终交付成果是一份测试报告。

history.summary: Etymonline记录的是deliverable的形容词历史：1727年已有“能够交付的”用法，由deliver加-able构成。这一记录说明其构词来源，并未在该条目中给出现代项目管理名词“交付成果”的首次使用年代。

cambridge.definitionEn: a failure to happen or finish on time:

learning.title: 未能按时发生或完成；延误
learning.en: a failure to happen or finish on time:
learning.example: Weekly checks revealed further slippage.
learning.zh: 每周检查发现进度进一步延误。

history.summary: slippage由slip加-age构成，1850年已有表示滑动行为的记录。词条还记载到20世纪初机械领域表示滑动量的用法；当前的进度延误义与这份早期记录分开理解。

cambridge.definitionEn: the act of ending something:

learning.title: 结束；终结某项事务
learning.en: the act of ending something:
learning.example: Closure requires evidence of completion.
learning.zh: 结案需要完成证据。

history.summary: closure在14世纪末可指屏障或围栏，经古法语上溯表示关闭的拉丁语词形。15世纪初已有关闭、使某事结束的意思，后来也用于议会终止辩论及心理学中形成完整整体的概念。

cambridge.definitionEn: a list of matters to be discussed at a meeting:

learning.title: 会议上待讨论的事项清单
learning.en: a list of matters to be discussed at a meeting:
learning.example: Add staffing to tomorrow's agenda.
learning.zh: 把人员配置加入明天的议程。

history.summary: agenda来自拉丁语表示待办之事的复数形式。17世纪中叶早期英语用例带有神学背景；Etymonline记录，表示会议上待处理事项的现代用法到1882年已出现。

cambridge.definitionEn: the situation within which something exists or happens, and that can help explain it:

learning.title: 事情存在或发生的背景情况
learning.en: the situation within which something exists or happens, and that can help explain it:
learning.example: The chart needs more context.
learning.zh: 这张图需要更多背景信息。

history.summary: context在15世纪初可指一整篇文字或编纂文本。拉丁语来源含有连接、交织的意思；到16世纪，英语中发展出某段话前后相连的文字这一用法，也就是上下文。

cambridge.definitionEn: to make something clear or easier to understand by giving more details or a simpler explanation:

learning.title: 通过细节或解释使事情更清楚
learning.en: to make something clear or easier to understand by giving more details or a simpler explanation:
learning.example: Please clarify the payment terms.
learning.zh: 请澄清付款条件。

history.summary: clarify来自法语及拉丁语中使之清楚、明亮的构词。英语早期也有彰显、使知晓等现已不用的意义，后来用于澄清液体；使表达容易理解的比喻义另有较晚记录。

cambridge.definitionEn: to prove or state the truth of something that was previously not completely certain:

learning.title: 证实；确认原先尚不确定的事情
learning.en: to prove or state the truth of something that was previously not completely certain:
learning.example: Confirm the quantity before ordering.
learning.zh: 下单前确认数量。

history.summary: confirm在13世纪中叶已用于批准、使法律行为有效，拉丁语来源的核心是使牢固、加强。随后出现加强和使事情确定、核实真实性的用法，体现从牢固到确认的语义发展。

cambridge.definitionEn: to explain or describe something clearly and exactly:

learning.title: 清楚且准确地说明
learning.en: to explain or describe something clearly and exactly:
learning.example: The contract specifies delivery dates.
learning.zh: 合同明确规定交货日期。

history.summary: specify在14世纪初已有说清楚、表达的用法，随后用于明确点名某人或某物。它经法语和晚期拉丁语进入英语，与表示具体、特定的specific属于同一词族。

cambridge.definitionEn: to add more information to or explain something that you have said:

learning.title: 进一步补充信息或详细解释
learning.en: to add more information to or explain something that you have said:
learning.example: Could you elaborate on that risk?
learning.zh: 你能详细说明那项风险吗？

history.summary: elaborate的形容词早期表示经过劳动精制，继而指制作细致、内容详尽。动词约1600年已有记录，17世纪初用于细致展开或加工；其拉丁语来源与付出努力、做出成果有关。

cambridge.definitionEn: to provide a clear statement of the important points:

learning.title: 清楚概述主要要点
learning.en: to provide a clear statement of the important points:
learning.example: Summarize the findings in one paragraph.
learning.zh: 用一段话概括调查结果。

history.summary: summarize由summary加动词后缀-ize构成。Etymonline将1837年的美式英语记录列为早期用例，意思是把内容作成概要、以简短形式陈述要点。

cambridge.definitionEn: to repeat the main points of an explanation or a description:

learning.title: 简要重复主要内容
learning.en: to repeat the main points of an explanation or a description:
learning.example: Let's recap yesterday's decisions.
learning.zh: 我们来简要回顾昨天的决定。

history.summary: recap存在不同构词来源：重新加盖的意义由re-和cap组成，早期也用于给轮胎翻新。表示概括、回顾时则是recapitulate的缩略形式，词条记录这一缩略用法到1907年已出现。

cambridge.definitionEn: to be the same or similar, or to agree with each other; to make two things do this:

learning.title: 彼此一致；使相互协调
learning.en: to be the same or similar, or to agree with each other; to make two things do this:
learning.example: Align the forecast with actual orders.
learning.zh: 使预测与实际订单相符。

history.summary: align的法语来源原本表示把东西排成一条线，核心词根与line有关。英语后来用于归入同一阵线；国际政治中的结盟或立场一致用法，词条记录于20世纪。

cambridge.definitionEn: a generally accepted opinion or decision among a group of people:

learning.title: 群体普遍接受的意见或决定
learning.en: a generally accepted opinion or decision among a group of people:
learning.example: There is no consensus on pricing.
learning.zh: 定价问题尚无共识。

history.summary: consensus来自拉丁语中共同感受、意见相合的表达。19世纪中叶的早期记录用于生理学，描述各部分协调；随后明确用于人们在意见上的普遍一致。

cambridge.definitionEn: a worried or nervous feeling about something, or something that makes you feel worried:

learning.title: 担忧；引起担忧的事情
learning.en: a worried or nervous feeling about something, or something that makes you feel worried:
learning.example: Her concern about safety was valid.
learning.zh: 她对安全的担忧有道理。

history.summary: concern的动词在15世纪已有涉及、关联的意思，后来发展出影响利益、使人忧虑的用法。名词形成较晚，可表示与某人相关的事、关切，也曾发展出商业机构这一不同用法。

cambridge.definitionEn: a feeling or expression of opposition, dislike, or disapproval:

learning.title: 反对或不赞同的表达
learning.en: a feeling or expression of opposition, dislike, or disapproval:
learning.example: The supplier raised an objection.
learning.zh: 供应商提出了反对意见。

history.summary: objection在14世纪末已有反驳某个命题或推理的意思。它经法语上溯拉丁语中提出、置于面前及反对的构词，因此早期就与论辩中的反对意见有关。

cambridge.definitionEn: the reasons or intentions that cause a particular set of beliefs or actions:

learning.title: 某种信念或行动背后的理由
learning.en: the reasons or intentions that cause a particular set of beliefs or actions:
learning.example: Record the rationale for each exception.
learning.zh: 记录每项例外的理由。

history.summary: rationale在17世纪中叶用于阐明原理，来自与理性、理由有关的拉丁语词形。随后扩展为某件事的根本理由、合理依据或动机。

cambridge.definitionEn: a suggestion, sometimes a written one:

learning.title: 提出供考虑的建议
learning.en: a suggestion, sometimes a written one:
learning.example: The proposal includes a training budget.
learning.zh: 提案包含培训预算。

history.summary: proposal由propose加名词后缀-al构成，17世纪中叶用于提出供接受的计划或方案。表示求婚提议的专门用法也有较晚的独立记录，不是这个词唯一的含义。

cambridge.definitionEn: something that is different, esp. from what is usual; a choice:

learning.title: 另一种可选择的办法或事物
learning.en: something that is different, esp. from what is usual; a choice:
learning.example: We need a cheaper alternative.
learning.zh: 我们需要一个成本更低的替代方案。

history.summary: alternative的来源与轮流、一个接一个的拉丁语词族有关。形容词在16世纪末可表示两者择一，名词随后用于相互排斥的命题；19世纪逐渐出现行动方案和可选对象等用法。

cambridge.definitionEn: an agreement in an argument in which the people involved reduce their demands or change their opinion in order to agree:

learning.title: 通过双方让步达成的协议
learning.en: an agreement in an argument in which the people involved reduce their demands or change their opinion in order to agree:
learning.example: The compromise satisfied both departments.
learning.zh: 折中方案让两个部门都满意。

history.summary: compromise在15世纪初原指双方共同承诺接受仲裁结果。随后意义扩展到以相互让步解决分歧，以及由此达成的协议；动词另有使声誉或安全受损的不同发展。

cambridge.definitionEn: to have formal discussions with someone in order to reach an agreement with them:

learning.title: 通过正式讨论寻求协议
learning.en: to have formal discussions with someone in order to reach an agreement with them:
learning.example: They negotiated a longer warranty.
learning.zh: 他们谈妥了更长的保修期。

history.summary: negotiate在16世纪末已用于为取得共同协议而沟通。其拉丁语来源与经商、处理事务有关；更晚出现成功应付困难或通过障碍等扩展用法。

cambridge.definitionEn: to end a speech, meeting, or piece of writing:

learning.title: 结束讲话、会议或文字
learning.en: to end a speech, meeting, or piece of writing:
learning.example: We concluded that repairs were necessary.
learning.zh: 我们得出结论，维修是必要的。

history.summary: conclude的拉丁语来源含有关闭、围合的意思。英语中早期与结束争论有关，14世纪末已有推断、作出判断，以及使事情终结的用法，因而“得出结论”和“结束”都很早。

cambridge.definitionEn: to record the details of an event, a process, etc.:

learning.title: 记录事件或过程的细节
learning.en: to record the details of an event, a process, etc.:
learning.example: Document every approved design change.
learning.zh: 记录每项获批的设计变更。

history.summary: document的名词来源与教导、示例、证明有关，后来指能提供证据的书面文件。动词早期曾表示权威地教导，18世纪初已有用文件证据支持某事的意思。

cambridge.definitionEn: to notice or understand the difference between two things, or to make one person or thing seem different from another:

learning.title: 识别差别；使区别显明
learning.en: to notice or understand the difference between two things, or to make one person or thing seem different from another:
learning.example: Distinguish fixed costs from variable costs.
learning.zh: 区分固定成本与变动成本。

history.summary: distinguish经法语或拉丁语进入英语，16世纪已有识别差异的用法，其来源与分开、标明界限有关。词条对更早的字面构词解释保留学术分歧，不宜把某一种形象解释当成确定事实。

cambridge.definitionEn: to say or think that something is the result of a particular thing:

learning.title: 将某事归因于特定因素
learning.en: to say or think that something is the result of a particular thing:
learning.example: They attributed the savings to automation.
learning.zh: 他们把节省归因于自动化。

history.summary: attribute的动词在14世纪末有分配、赋予之义，来自拉丁语中分配给、托付给的表达，也包含归于或归因的比喻用法。名词指被赋予的性质，重音位置与动词不同。

cambridge.definitionEn: to be one of the reasons why something happens:

learning.title: 成为某事发生的原因之一
learning.en: to be one of the reasons why something happens:
learning.example: Better lighting contributes to safer work.
learning.zh: 更好的照明有助于安全作业。

history.summary: contribute在16世纪初表示与他人共同给予或提供，拉丁语来源包含集合、增加和分配的含义。17世纪已有比喻用法，逐渐可用于金钱以外的贡献或促成因素。

cambridge.definitionEn: to show, point, or make clear in another way:

learning.title: 显示、指出或说明
learning.en: to show, point, or make clear in another way:
learning.example: The results indicate a quality problem.
learning.zh: 结果显示存在质量问题。

history.summary: indicate在17世纪中叶已有指出的用法，与拉丁语中指明、展示的词形相连。18世纪初已有提供暗示、构成推断依据的意义，区别于直接作出充分证明。

cambridge.definitionEn: to communicate an idea or feeling without saying it directly:

learning.title: 不直接说出而传达某个意思
learning.en: to communicate an idea or feeling without saying it directly:
learning.example: Silence does not imply consent.
learning.zh: 沉默不意味着同意。

history.summary: imply在14世纪末可指包裹、缠绕，其拉丁语来源与折叠、卷入有关。约1400年已有包含未明说逻辑后果的意思，16世纪又出现暗示用法；与读者作推断的infer不同。

cambridge.definitionEn: to give or to be a good reason for:

learning.title: 为某事提供充分或合理的理由
learning.en: to give or to be a good reason for:
learning.example: The savings justify the investment.
learning.zh: 节省金额证明这项投资合理。

history.summary: justify约1300年用于施行正义，14世纪末已有说明某事公正或正确的意思。其来源结合了公正与使成为的构词；后来还用于证明无罪及排版中把文字调整整齐。

cambridge.definitionEn: to show the meaning or truth of something more clearly, especially by giving examples:

learning.title: 通过例子更清楚地说明
learning.en: to show the meaning or truth of something more clearly, especially by giving examples:
learning.example: The diagram illustrates the approval flow.
learning.zh: 示意图说明了审批流程。

history.summary: illustrate在16世纪初有照亮的意思，17世纪初用于借例子讲解。随后也指提供图片以解释或装饰，因此举例说明和插图两种现代用法有各自的历史记录。

cambridge.definitionEn: to decide what the meaning of something is:

learning.title: 判断或解释某事的含义
learning.en: to decide what the meaning of something is:
learning.example: Different teams interpret the rule differently.
learning.zh: 不同团队对规则的解读不同。

history.summary: interpret在14世纪末已用于阐明意义，使内容明确，经法语和拉丁语进入英语。拉丁语相关名词可指中间人或译者；词条对其第二部分更早词根的解释保留不同观点。

cambridge.definitionEn: facts, information, documents, etc. that give reason to believe that something is true:

learning.title: 支持某事属实的事实或资料
learning.en: facts, information, documents, etc. that give reason to believe that something is true:
learning.example: Keep evidence of the inspection.
learning.zh: 保留检验的证据。

history.summary: evidence约1300年用于可供推断的外在表现，来源与明显、清楚地呈现有关。随后发展为相信某事的依据；法律上的证据意义在约1500年前后有记录。

cambridge.definitionEn: the effect that an action or decision will have on something else in the future:

learning.title: 某项行动或决定未来产生的影响
learning.en: the effect that an action or decision will have on something else in the future:
learning.example: Consider the financial implications first.
learning.zh: 先考虑财务影响。

history.summary: implication在15世纪初指缠结或相互交织的状态，与imply同属表示卷入、折叠的拉丁语词族。16世纪中叶已有未明说但可由观察推知之意；现代具体影响须结合用法理解。

cambridge.definitionEn: a fact or situation that influences the result of something:

learning.title: 影响某个结果的因素
learning.en: a fact or situation that influences the result of something:
learning.example: Distance is another cost factor.
learning.zh: 距离是另一个成本因素。

history.summary: factor早期可指商业代理人，拉丁语来源是做事者、制作者。数学中相乘因子的意义在17世纪出现，后来由此发展出能造成某个结果的条件或因素。

cambridge.definitionEn: the degree to which something happens or is likely to happen:

learning.title: 发生或影响所达到的程度
learning.en: the degree to which something happens or is likely to happen:
learning.example: We underestimated the extent of damage.
learning.zh: 我们低估了损坏程度。

history.summary: extent约1300年与财产估价、土地税额有关，经法语上溯表示展开、延伸的拉丁语动词。到16世纪末，已有某事延伸到何种程度这一较一般的用法。

cambridge.definitionEn: the chance that something will happen:

learning.title: 某事发生的可能性
learning.en: the chance that something will happen:
learning.example: The likelihood of delay remains high.
learning.zh: 延误的可能性仍很高。

history.summary: likelihood由likely加-hood构成。14世纪末早期可表示相似，15世纪中叶开始出现概率、可能状态的意义，不应把今天的概率义直接当成最初含义。

cambridge.definitionEn: a situation in which something is not known, or something that is not known or certain:

learning.title: 未知或尚未确定的情况
learning.en: a situation in which something is not known, or something that is not known or certain:
learning.example: Uncertainty makes long-term planning difficult.
learning.zh: 不确定性使长期规划困难。

history.summary: uncertainty在14世纪末已有记录，由uncertain加名词后缀-ty构成。早期涵盖不确定、怀疑、不可靠以及尚未明确知道的状态，与现代核心用法相近。

cambridge.definitionEn: a warning to consider something before taking any more action, or a statement that limits a more general statement:

learning.title: 需要留意的警告或限定说明
learning.en: a warning to consider something before taking any more action, or a statement that limits a more general statement:
learning.example: Read the caveat below the chart.
learning.zh: 阅读图表下方的注意事项。

history.summary: caveat直接来自拉丁语中提醒对方当心的表达，16世纪中叶作为英语名词表示警告、注意提示。17世纪又出现法律上公开警告以阻止某种行动的专门含义。

cambridge.definitionEn: in agreement with other facts or with typical or previous behaviour, or having the same principles as something else:

learning.title: 与事实、行为或原则相符
learning.en: in agreement with other facts or with typical or previous behaviour, or having the same principles as something else:
learning.example: The readings are consistent across shifts.
learning.zh: 各班次的读数一致。

history.summary: consistent来源于拉丁语中站稳、保持位置的词形。17世纪出现与某事相合、一致的意义，18世纪进一步用于表现出持续一致性；词族也保留与实体稠度有关的用法。

cambridge.definitionEn: a difference between two things that should be the same:

learning.title: 本应相同的两者之间的不一致
learning.en: a difference between two things that should be the same:
learning.example: Investigate the discrepancy in inventory records.
learning.zh: 调查库存记录中的差异。

history.summary: discrepancy在15世纪中叶已表示事实或意见上的差异，其拉丁语来源字面上与声音不一致有关。现代拼写形式到17世纪初出现，常用于本应相符的信息之间的出入。

cambridge.definitionEn: a statement that you strongly believe is true:

learning.title: 坚信为真的陈述或主张
learning.en: a statement that you strongly believe is true:
learning.example: That assertion needs independent verification.
learning.zh: 那项断言需要独立核实。

history.summary: assertion在15世纪初可指声明、确认，经法语或拉丁语传入英语，其词族涉及宣称、认领。15世纪中叶也有缺少支持的陈述这一用法；提出主张并不自动等于已有证据。

cambridge.definitionEn: in a way that is suggested but not communicated directly:

learning.title: 通过暗含而非明说的方式
learning.en: in a way that is suggested but not communicated directly:
learning.example: The estimate implicitly includes overtime.
learning.zh: 估算隐含地计入了加班。

history.summary: implicitly由implicit加副词后缀-ly构成，约1600年已有通过暗示表达的意思。17世纪中叶另有毫不怀疑、完全信任的用法，两种意义需分别辨认。

cambridge.definitionEn: in an opposite way:

learning.title: 以相反的方式；反过来说
learning.en: in an opposite way:
learning.example: Higher prices reduce demand; conversely, discounts encourage purchases.
learning.zh: 涨价压低需求；反之，折扣促进购买。

history.summary: 这里引用组成词converse的形容词历史：16世纪已有反转、互换的数学用法，来源于表示转向的拉丁语词形，后来指方向相反。Etymonline将conversely列为相关派生形式；这不是独立副词条目的首见年代。

cambridge.definitionEn: to accept, admit, or recognize something, or the truth or existence of something:

learning.title: 承认或认可某事的真实性或存在
learning.en: to accept, admit, or recognize something, or the truth or existence of something:
learning.example: Acknowledge the error in your report.
learning.zh: 在报告中承认错误。

history.summary: acknowledge形成于两个中古英语动词的合流，两者都涉及承认、表明知道。15世纪末已有现代词形的记录，16世纪逐渐取代旧形式；拼写中的c不是原来构词中的固定组成。

cambridge.definitionEn: lasting for a long time or difficult to get rid of:

learning.title: 长期持续或难以消除的
learning.en: lasting for a long time or difficult to get rid of:
learning.example: Persistent shortages disrupted the schedule.
learning.zh: 持续短缺打乱了日程。

history.summary: persistent在18世纪初早期多见于植物学，表示保持、持续存在，与坚持的拉丁语词族相连。19世纪又明确用于面对反对或警告仍继续的行为。

cambridge.definitionEn: real but not immediately obvious:

learning.title: 实际存在但不立即显明的
learning.en: real but not immediately obvious:
learning.example: The underlying assumptions remain unchanged.
learning.zh: 基本假设仍未改变。

history.summary: underlying是underlie的现在分词形容词，17世纪初用于位于下方、起支撑作用。表示根本、基础性的比喻用法，词条记录到19世纪中叶已出现。

cambridge.definitionEn: the state of depending on or trusting in something or someone:

learning.title: 依靠或信赖某人某事的状态
learning.en: the state of depending on or trusting in something or someone:
learning.example: Reduce reliance on temporary staff.
learning.zh: 减少对临时员工的依赖。

history.summary: reliance约1600年已有记录，由rely加名词后缀-ance构成，表示依靠的行为或处于依赖状态。该词条本身是较短的构词说明，不额外提供某个现代行业用法的历史。

cambridge.definitionEn: a particular way of considering something:

learning.title: 看待某件事的角度或方式
learning.en: a particular way of considering something:
learning.example: Consider the issue from a customer perspective.
learning.zh: 从客户角度考虑这个问题。

history.summary: perspective在14世纪末与光学有关，来源与仔细观察、看穿的拉丁语词形相连。16世纪用于画面中表现距离和深度，随后发展出把各部分关系放在适当位置及思想视角的比喻义。

cambridge.definitionEn: tending to cause disagreements that separate people into opposing groups:

learning.title: 容易造成分歧并使人分成对立阵营的
learning.en: tending to cause disagreements that separate people into opposing groups:
learning.example: The divisive policy split the committee.
learning.zh: 这项引发分歧的政策使委员会分裂。

history.summary: divisive约1600年表示具有分开、划分的性质，由表示分割的拉丁语词干加-ive构成。17世纪中叶已有制造分裂、引起不和的意义。

cambridge.definitionEn: an unfair personal opinion that influences your judgment:

learning.title: 影响判断的不公正个人倾向
learning.en: an unfair personal opinion that influences your judgment:
learning.example: Anonymous reviews can reduce personal bias.
learning.zh: 匿名评审可减少个人偏见。

history.summary: bias在16世纪初表示斜线或倾斜，来自法语，但更早来源并不完全确定。它曾用于滚木球运动中使球偏转的形状或重心，随后产生思想偏向一侧以及偏见的比喻义。
